claim: James Hamish says Tottenham tried to force Richarlison out by leaving him out of the lineup, and the club chose not to formally release him despite him being surplus; he remains frozen out of the squad.
quote: I said there was a chance they would leave him out of the lineup and try to force him to leave. That's what they were trying to do.

claim: James Hamish argues Tottenham now have enough attacking depth (Solanke, Marmoush, Sávio, Kudus, Tel, Mudryk) that even if two first-choice forwards were injured together, they would not need to recall Richarlison.
quote: Tottenham have a bunch of options now, so they won't have to go back to Richarlison.

claim: Focal already has his Triple Captain chip active for Gameweek 4, having originally planned to save it but using it instead of the wildcard slot he ended up taking last week.
quote: I've got the chip active, triple captain's active for gameweek four

claim: Focal is transferring Foden out for Palmer this week, spending his remaining bank on the move with two free transfers banked.
quote: Foden to Palmer is the planned transfer. I'm going to use the money in the bank towards that

claim: Focal is triple-captaining Palmer this gameweek and making João Pedro vice-captain instead.
quote: I'm going to be bringing Palmer in and swapping the captaincy to him.

claim: Focal cites fpl.page's projected GW4 team goals with Chelsea top at 2.9, ahead of Liverpool 2.5 and Arsenal/Man City 1.9, as part of the case for a Chelsea captain.
quote: Chelsea's 2.9 is top this week. Then it's Liverpool with 2.5. Arsenal, Man City are on 1.9.

claim: Focal calls Hull's defensive record unsustainable: three clean sheets from three games despite conceding over 5 expected goals, 13th-best in the league for xGC.
quote: Hull have kept three clean sheets in their opening three. It's been a massive overperformance. Over five expected goals conceded, but none have gone in.

claim: Focal cites GW4 clean sheet odds: Arsenal top at 50%, Chelsea 46%, Liverpool 34%, Palace and Spurs 32%, Brighton and Villa 31%.
quote: Arsenal are top of the Gameweek 4 clean sheet. Ours is given a 50% chance. Chelsea second, 46%. Liverpool 34%. Palace and Spurs 32%.

claim: Focal is starting Raya at 6.0m, judging Arsenal's defence needs to keep delivering clean sheets consistently to justify the price.
quote: Raya was a really difficult call as well, cuz 6 mil is a lot, and he needs to be clocking in regular clean sheets very consistently to justify that.

claim: Focal passed on Calafiori despite liking his upside, flagging a small chance he becomes a rotation risk at some point down the line.
quote: It might not happen, but at some point in the future, he may or may not become a rotation risk.

claim: Focal went for Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Chalobah as solid budget defenders instead of Calafiori.
quote: I decided to get ahead of that possibility and go for some other solid defenders like Van Hecke, De Cuyper, and Chalobah.

claim: Focal notes De Cuyper takes Brighton's corners from the right side.
quote: he does take corners from the right side

claim: Focal says owning both De Cuyper and Gross covers every Brighton dead ball, with De Cuyper's upside boosted by playing out of position on the left.
quote: if you've got him and Gross, you've got every dead ball covered on your team, and the upside is big when he's playing out of position left wing

claim: Focal expects Mitoma to still be some time away from returning, which keeps De Cuyper's starting role secure in the meantime.
quote: The hope is that Mitoma is still a while away from returning.

claim: Focal flags a favourable Brighton fixture swing benefiting De Cuyper: away to Sunderland in Gameweek 6 and possibly Palace at home in Gameweek 7.
quote: you get the benefit of Sondergard in Gameweek 6, and also you get Palace home in Gameweek 7, maybe

claim: Focal says De Cuyper is sellable before his good fixture run arrives if his minutes situation changes.
quote: if it comes to it, he's sellable before then

claim: Focal has Rogers coming into his starting XI this week, having previously started Palmer against Arsenal instead of him.
quote: the combination there was to have Palmer, and start him against Arsenal, and then it's Rodgers that comes in this week

claim: Focal rates a fully fit Saka as one of the best assets in the game and a set-and-forget pick.
quote: A fully fit Saka is one of the best FPL assets in the game.

claim: Focal expects the FPL community to gradually move away from owning the 15.5m Haaland toward a Saka/Palmer/Bruno three-man premium midfield, and thinks he will likely end up there himself.
quote: I think it's going to lead to people moving to Saka, Palmer, Bruno three-man midfield.

claim: Focal reports apparent Fulham unrest: Smith Rowe and Iwobi have removed Fulham from Instagram, Kevin posted a cryptic story, and an unresolved player is said to be unhappy about not getting opportunities.
quote: Smith Rowe removes Fulham from his Instagram completely. Iwobi the same. Kevin posts a cryptic story on his Instagram.

claim: Focal thinks this could be a strong week for Liverpool and says to definitely keep Isak and Gakpo if they play.
quote: if you've got Isak and plays, maybe Gakpo over as well, definitely keep those.

claim: Focal expects Man City's attackers to keep rotating and is avoiding City assets for now aside from Haaland, though he flags Enzo as one worth watching.
quote: Maybe Enzo is actually the one worth looking at. I'm going to totally avoid for now, except for Haaland.

claim: Focal confirms the plan to sell Foden this week is locked in.
quote: The plan was always to sell Foden this week, so that move is locked in.

claim: Focal calls Wissa's trip to Leeds a tough fixture, noting Leeds have started the season well including good business on an unresolved signing plus Trafford.
quote: It's a tough fixture for Wissa. He's playing Leeds away and they've started the season really well, Leeds.

claim: Focal is starting Wissa despite the tough fixture, saying none of his bench options are better this week.
quote: I don't like any of the bench players more than Wissa this week though, so he's starting.

claim: Focal cites Haaland's Manchester derby record of 11 goal involvements (8 goals, 3 assists) in 7 appearances as background for his captaincy quality, though he isn't captaining him this week.

claim: Focal cites a captaincy ratings widget with Palmer top on five stars, João Pedro and Rogers on three, and Haaland and Saka both on two.

claim: Focal says he won't finalize his captaincy call until Man City's home lineup against Ipswich is confirmed.
quote: Not going to be doing anything before Man City play Ipswich home though.

claim: Focal's GW4 bench is Bentley, Chalobah, Sangaré and Mendy.
quote: The bench is Bentley, Chalobah, Sangaré, and Mendy.

claim: Focal plans to roll his transfer in Gameweek 5 with no forced moves, and could bench-swap his keeper for Chalobah or Gross for an unresolved bench midfielder to chase defensive-contribution points given Brighton face Arsenal.

claim: Focal plans to eventually sell an unresolved defender for Bournemouth's Senesi around Gameweek 7, with Mendy as bench insurance in the meantime given Bournemouth's tricky fixture the week before.

claim: Focal sketches a speculative Gameweek 8-9 pivot away from Haaland toward Gonzalo, Bruno and Gibbs-White, ending with a midfield of five penalty-takers, stressing it is far out and not locked in.

claim: Focal still has his Free Hit chip available and thinks it could be primed for Gameweek 14 or 16, though he's unsure which.
